result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers give the same sound advice: file clear matches automatically, send uncertain cases for review, keep a log and digest with undo, and be stricter if client folders are shared. B is tighter but invents figures ('20–30% of receipts', 'a 2-minute skim'). A avoids made-up numbers and says to decide from real results, though it adds some extra features (learning rules, pause switch, status line) and runs longer. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers recommend auto-filing clear matches and asking only about uncertain ones, and both raise the shared-folder confidentiality caveat. B names the specific uncertain cases (no match, two possible clients, unreadable PDF), puts an Undo button in the digest and avoids guessing numbers. A makes up a 20–30% review rate and a 2-minute skim time. B loses some points on brevity and focus because it adds extras like learning from corrections, a pause switch and a status line.
